Name: Talisman's South Park Ontology Explainer, with a rulebook underneath
Description: Jessica Talisman's interactive South Park ontology explainer rebuilt on one rulebook: the same facts, rule switches and conclusions in Postgres, TypeScript, Python, Excel, OWL and documentation in 16 languages.

ProjectSettings.Name: project-name
ProjectSettings.Value: Talisman's South Park Ontology Explainer, with a rulebook underneath

ProjectTranspilers.Name: compile-rulebook
ProjectTranspilers.Description: Bake every calculated, lookup and aggregation value into the hub's own data rows; the conformance harness reads its answer keys from them.

ProjectTranspilers.Name: rulebooktopostgres
ProjectTranspilers.Description: Postgres schema, vw_* views and seed data from the rulebook.

ProjectTranspilers.Name: rulebooktotypescript
ProjectTranspilers.Description: TypeScript substrate: the app's TypeScript engine and the conformance harness run it.

ProjectTranspilers.Name: rulebooktoxlsx
ProjectTranspilers.Description: Excel workbook with every rule as a live formula.

ProjectTranspilers.Name: rulebooktoowl
ProjectTranspilers.Description: OWL ontology, individuals and SHACL rules: the app's OWL engine and the conformance harness run them.

ProjectTranspilers.Name: rulebooktorulespeak
ProjectTranspilers.Description: Plain-language documentation of every rule, in every language the tool offers.

ProjectTranspilers.Name: rulebooktoexplainerdag
ProjectTranspilers.Description: Explainer: every derived value's rule and witness down to ground truth, in 16 languages.

ProjectTranspilers.Name: explainertypescript
ProjectTranspilers.Description: A second copy of the TypeScript substrate inside the explainer's folder, where the explainer looks for it to compute witnesses in the page.

ProjectTranspilers.Name: effortlessrulebookeditor
ProjectTranspilers.Description: The generated rulebook editor: its own Postgres, API and admin UI in a container (./start.sh --editor).

ProjectTranspilers.Name: concept-rulebook
ProjectTranspilers.Description: Write the concept rulebook: the same ontology as ordinary tables (individuals, a table per class, a table or a column per property, ERBTables and ERBFields), from the hub compile-rulebook just baked. orchestration/ontology_form.py is the mapping; the script is committed executable and takes no arguments. The app's Save writes the same file from the live rows.

ProjectTranspilers.Name: conceptrulebookeditor
ProjectTranspilers.Description: The generated rulebook editor on the concept rulebook: its own Postgres, API and admin UI in a second container (./start.sh --concept-editor). Its Save rewrites the concept rulebook file; the app's Concepts page loads that file back into the ontology.

ProjectTranspilers.Name: conceptrulebooktorulespeak
ProjectTranspilers.Description: The concept rulebook's own documentation: the same tool as rulebooktorulespeak, on the concept rulebook the concept-rulebook step just wrote. The concept form's tools panel links to it.

ProjectTranspilers.Name: conceptrulebooktoexplainerdag
ProjectTranspilers.Description: The concept rulebook's own explainer: the same tool as rulebooktoexplainerdag, on the concept rulebook. The concept form's tools panel links to it.

ProjectTranspilers.Name: conceptexplainertypescript
ProjectTranspilers.Description: The TypeScript substrate of the concept rulebook inside its explainer's folder, where the explainer looks for it to compute witnesses in the page (as explainertypescript does for the rulebook).

ProjectTranspilers.Name: init-db
ProjectTranspilers.Description: Load the generated SQL into the project database. Last on purpose: the CLI regenerates reset-rulebook-db.sh without its executable bit (cr-20-02), so this -exec step fails on most builds; scripts/erb_project.py --reset-db runs it with bash.
